skill_gap.name: no reference-game resolution
skill_gap.why: The entire prompt is 'like <named Roblox game>'. The genre file resolves two such names by hand — Brookhaven to Life, Bloxburg to Home Builder — but there is no rule for any other title, and nothing tells you whether to use outside knowledge of a game you happen to recognise. So the reference collapses to the single word 'rp' and everything specific about the named game is dropped, which for this bucket is most of the request.

notes_for_us: The genre file's 'Typical shapes' line lists bare IDs, but emit requires shape.type and shape.name split from a '**Type (Flavor Name)**' row that only shapes.md holds — and the skill says not to load shapes.md when a typical shape fits. Following both rules makes the shape emit form unfillable; I emitted nulls.

Step 5's scale row only fires when the prompt 'names an extent without naming what lives in it'. A three-word prompt names neither, so the trigger never fires and the assumed band ships with no question covering it, even though block versus district changes this map materially.

Theme: layout-intake says infer where possible but emit null on silence. A named reference game is a strong theme signal that is not the prompt speaking, and there is no guidance on whether recognising the reference counts as inference. I emitted null.

The Life preset produces no layout_placement entries at all — all three of its options are image-only — so a claimable-housing town ships with no claim markers, spawn or plot volumes. Nothing in the skill flags an empty layout stream as worth a second look.

'Take the whole preset' from the eval brief and 'never inject an option the user did not choose' from genre-choice point opposite ways on a prompt this terse: the user chose nothing, so every option in the handoff is technically uninvited.
